notes.title: Today

notes.content:
$pdf = new Fpdi();

Creates a brand-new, empty PDF document. This is the output we're building — it starts with zero pages. Fpdi is special: it's a normal PDF-writing class (like FPDF) that's also able to read pages out of existing PDF files and reuse them as content.

$pageCount = $pdf->setSourceFile(StreamReader::createByString($pdfContent));

For each invoice's raw bytes: StreamReader::createByString($pdfContent) wraps the byte string in an in-memory reader (so FPDI can parse it without writing it to a temp file on disk first). $pdf->setSourceFile(...) parses that PDF and returns how many pages it has ($pageCount).

importPage($pageNumber) parses that one page's content and hands back an internal template ID. This doesn't add anything to the output yet — it's just "here's page 3 of invoice A, ready to be reused."

- getTemplateSize($templateId) reads that page's actual width/height/orientation. This matters because not every invoice PDF is guaranteed to be identical page size — this keeps each page in the merged file at its own original dimensions instead of stretching/cropping.

- AddPage($orientation, [$width, $height]) starts a new blank page in the output document, sized to match.

- useTemplate($templateId) stamps that imported page's content onto the new blank page, full-bleed.
